name: Light Blue Grey
lede: Light Blue Grey is a light shade of [[blue-grey|blue-grey]], one of Robert Ridgway's working names built by the plain grammar of modifier plus base color.

sections.title: A modifier, not a new color
sections.body: Light Blue Grey joins the modifier *light* to the base color [[blue-grey]], raising the value of an already desaturated hue [1][4]. The name shows up in several of our library's systems at once, including CSS, Wikipedia's X11 table, and the crowd-labeled xkcd survey, besides Ridgway and ISCC-NBS [1][2][4]. The systems do not all agree on the exact hex: one alternate reading lands closer to #B7C9E2, a cooler and paler blue than the #A4AAB6 shown here [4]. The ISCC-NBS system calls the matching block, 185, 'pale blue,' a Delta-E of 6.4 from this article's value [2]. The nearest named colors on file are [[pale-payne-s-grey]] and [[burn-blue]], at 3.9 and 4.8 ΔE [1][4].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this shade, as photographed, in 1.73% of 23,781 paintings, 411 paintings; within a single canvas it reads as a distinct area in 246 of them [3]. That ranks it more common than 74% of the archive's named colors [3]. It peaks in the 1900s, found in 2.2% of that century's 1,674 paintings, 1.6 times the expected rate [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a light, by lightness rank, in 57% of its 246 appearances [3]. Claude Monet is its most devoted painter by a wide margin, using it in 12 of his 50 works here, 13.8 times the baseline rate of the museums those paintings come from [3]. The earliest dated appearance is a painting from 1440, 472 years before the name's first documented record in 1912; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor and not a first [3]. It shares canvases with [[french-grey]] more often than chance, a lift of 4.6 [3].
